verses.1:1: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
verses.1:2: And the Lord gave into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah and some of the articles of the house of God. He brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and the articles he brought into the treasure house of his god.
verses.1:3: Then the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring some of the sons of Israel, both from the royal offspring and from the nobles,
verses.1:4: youths without any blemish, good in appearance, insightful in all wisdom, possessing knowledge, discerning in learning, and having the ability to stand in the king's palace—and to teach them the writings and language of the Chaldeans.
verses.1:5: The king assigned them a daily allotment from the king's fine food and from the wine he drank; they were to be trained for three years, and at the end of those years they were to stand before the king.
verses.1:6: And among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, from the sons of Judah.
verses.1:7: The commander of the eunuchs gave them names: Daniel he named Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
verses.1:8: But Daniel determined in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king's fine food or with the wine he drank; so he requested of the commander of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
verses.1:9: And God granted Daniel favor and mercy before the commander of the eunuchs.
verses.1:10: The commander of the eunuchs said to Daniel, "I fear my lord the king, who assigned your food and your drink. For why should he see your faces looking more haggard than the youths of your own age? Then you would make my head forfeit to the king."
verses.1:11: Then Daniel spoke to the attendant whom the commander of the eunuchs had assigned over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
verses.1:12: "Please test your servants for ten days, and let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
verses.1:13: Then let our appearance and the appearance of the youths who eat the king's fine food be observed before you, and deal with your servants according to what you see."
verses.1:14: He listened to them regarding this matter, and he tested them for ten days.
verses.1:15: At the end of ten days, their appearance looked better and they were fuller in flesh than all the youths who ate the king's fine food.
verses.1:16: So the attendant continued taking away their fine food and the wine for their drinking, and giving them vegetables.
verses.1:17: As for these four youths, God gave them learning and insight in all writings and wisdom, and Daniel had understanding in every vision and in dreams.
verses.1:18: At the end of the days when the king had commanded to bring them in, the commander of the eunuchs brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.1:19: The king spoke with them, and out of all of them no one was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; so they stood before the king.
verses.1:20: And in every matter of wise understanding that the king sought from them, he found them ten times superior to all the magicians, the enchanters, who were in all his kingdom.
verses.1:21: So Daniel remained until the first year of Cyrus the king.
verses.2:1: Now in the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, and his spirit became disturbed, and his sleep broke off from him.
verses.2:2: So the king commanded to call the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans to recount his dreams to the king; and they came and stood in the king's presence.
verses.2:3: The king spoke to them: "I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is disturbed to know the dream."
verses.2:4: And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: "King, live forever! Speak the dream to your servants, and we will report the interpretation."
verses.2:5: The king replied to the Chaldeans, saying, "My decree is settled: if you do not inform me of the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut to pieces, and your houses will be turned into a refuse heap.
verses.2:6: Yet if you report the dream and its interpretation, you will receive gifts, a reward, and great honor from me. So report to me the dream and its interpretation."
verses.2:7: They replied a second time, saying, "Let the king speak the dream to his servants, and we will report the interpretation."
verses.2:8: The king replied, saying, "I know for a fact that you are buying time, since you see that my decree is settled:
verses.2:9: that if you do not inform me of the dream, there is only one verdict for you; and you have conspired to speak false and corrupt talk before me until the season shifts. So speak the dream to me, and I will know that you are able to report its interpretation to me."
verses.2:10: The Chaldeans answered before the king and said, "There is not a person on the dry land who can report the king's matter, since no king, however great and powerful, has asked a thing like this of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
verses.2:11: The thing that the king is asking is difficult, and there is no one else who can report it before the king except gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh."
verses.2:12: At this the king grew enraged and exceedingly furious, and he commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:13: So the decree went out, and the wise men were to be killed; and they looked for Daniel and his companions, to kill them.
verses.2:14: Then Daniel responded with counsel and discretion to Arioch, the chief of the king's guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:15: He answered and said to Arioch, the king's officer, "Why is the decree from the king so harsh?" Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
verses.2:16: So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so that he might report the interpretation to the king.
verses.2:17: Then Daniel went home and informed Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions, of the matter,
verses.2:18: to seek mercy from the God of heaven regarding this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions might not perish along with the remaining wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:19: Then in a night vision the mystery was uncovered to Daniel, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
verses.2:20: Daniel replied, saying, "Let the name of God be blessed from eternity to eternity, for wisdom and might belong to Him.
verses.2:21: It is He who alters the times and the seasons; He deposes kings and raises up kings; He grants wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who know discernment.
verses.2:22: He uncovers the deep and secret things; He knows what lies in the darkness, and light resides with Him.
verses.2:23: To You, God of my fathers, I give thanks and offer praise, because You have granted me wisdom and might; and now You have informed me of what we asked from You, for You have disclosed to us the king's matter."
verses.2:24: Accordingly Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had assigned to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and spoke to him like this: "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon! Lead me into the king's presence, and I will report the interpretation to the king."
verses.2:25: Then Arioch brought Daniel in haste before the king and spoke to him like this: "I have found a man from the exiles of Judah who will inform the king of the interpretation."
verses.2:26: The king replied to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, saying, "Are you able to inform me of the dream I saw and its interpretation?"
verses.2:27: Daniel answered before the king and said, "The mystery that the king is asking about, no wise men, enchanters, magicians, or diviners are able to report to the king.
verses.2:28: Yet there is a God in heaven who uncovers mysteries, and He has disclosed to King Nebuchadnezzar what will occur at the end of days. Your dream and the visions of your head on your bed are these:
verses.2:29: As for you, King, your thoughts came up on your bed about what will occur after this; and He who uncovers mysteries has disclosed to you what will occur.
verses.2:30: As for me, it is not because of wisdom present in me beyond all the living that this mystery has been uncovered to me, but so that the interpretation would be disclosed to the king and you would understand the thoughts of your heart.
verses.2:31: You, King, were watching, and look—one huge statue! That immense statue, extraordinary in brilliance, stood opposite you, and its look was terrifying.
verses.2:32: As for that statue, its head was of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,
verses.2:33: its legs of iron, its feet part of iron and part of clay.
verses.2:34: You watched until a stone was broken off without hands, and it hit the statue on its feet of iron and clay and ground them to pieces.
verses.2:35: At that moment the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were ground down together and turned into chaff from the summer threshing floors; the wind swept them away, and no place at all was found for them. Yet the stone that hit the statue grew into a huge mountain and filled all the earth.
verses.2:36: This is the dream, and we will state its interpretation before the king.
verses.2:37: You, King, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has granted the kingship, the might, the power, and the honor;
verses.2:38: and wherever human beings, the wild animals of the field, and the birds of the heavens dwell, He has given them into your hand and set you as ruler over all of them. You yourself are the head of gold.
verses.2:39: After you another kingdom will arise, lower than you, and another, a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
verses.2:40: Then there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron, because iron grinds down and shatters everything; and like iron that smashes, it will grind down and smash all these.
verses.2:41: And in that you saw the feet and the toes part potter's clay and part iron, it will be a divided kingdom, yet something of the hardness of iron will be in it, just as you saw iron mingled with muddy clay.
verses.2:42: And the toes of the feet being part iron and part clay, a portion of the kingdom will be strong, and a portion of it will be fragile.
verses.2:43: And in that you saw iron mingled with muddy clay, they will mingle together through human seed, yet they will not cling to one another, this one to that one, just as iron does not mingle with clay.
verses.2:44: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be ruined, nor will the kingdom be passed on to another people; it will grind down and finish off all these kingdoms, while it itself will endure forever,
verses.2:45: just as you saw that a stone was broken off from the mountain without hands and ground down the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold. A great God has disclosed to the king what will occur after this; and certain is the dream, and reliable is its interpretation."
verses.2:46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and bowed down to Daniel, and he gave orders to present to him an offering and soothing fragrances.
verses.2:47: The king replied to Daniel, saying, "In truth, your God is God of gods, Lord of kings, and one who uncovers mysteries, because you were able to uncover this mystery."
verses.2:48: Then the king elevated Daniel and presented him with many large gifts, setting him as governor over the entire province of Babylon and chief of the prefects over all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:49: And Daniel petitioned the king, and he set Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained at the king's court.
verses.3:1: King Nebuchadnezzar made a statue of gold; its height was sixty cubits and its width six cubits. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
verses.3:2: Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent to gather the satraps, the prefects, and the governors, the advisers, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the rulers of the provinces to come to the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.3:3: Then the satraps, the prefects, and the governors, the advisers, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the rulers of the provinces gathered together for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood in front of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.3:4: And the herald called out loudly, "To you it is declared, peoples, nations, and languages,
verses.3:5: that at the time you hear the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every sort of music, you are to fall down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
verses.3:6: And whoever does not fall down and worship will at that very moment be thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire."
verses.3:7: Because of this, at that time, as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, trigon, harp, and every sort of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down, worshiping the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.3:8: Because of this, at that time, Chaldean men came forward and maliciously accused the Jews.
verses.3:9: They spoke up and said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "King, live forever!
verses.3:10: You, King, have issued a decree that every person who hears the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every sort of music is to fall down and worship the golden statue,
verses.3:11: and whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire.
verses.3:12: There are Jewish men whom you appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, King, have paid no regard to you; they do not serve your god, and they do not worship the golden statue that you have set up."
verses.3:13: Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and fury, ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought; then those men were brought before the king.
verses.3:14: Nebuchadnezzar spoke up and said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you are not serving my gods and are not worshiping the golden statue that I have set up?
verses.3:15: Now if you are ready, so that at the time you hear the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every sort of music, you fall down and worship the statue that I have made—but if you do not worship, at that very moment you will be thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire. And what god is there who will rescue you from my hands?"
verses.3:16: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered and said to the king, "Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to give you a reply concerning this.
verses.3:17: If it is so, our God whom we serve is able to rescue us; He will rescue us from the furnace of burning fire and from your hand, King.
verses.3:18: But if not, let it be known to you, King, that we do not serve your god and will not worship the golden statue that you have set up."
verses.3:19: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the expression of his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke up and gave orders to heat the furnace seven times more than it was customary to heat it.
verses.3:20: And he ordered mighty men of strength who were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the furnace of burning fire.
verses.3:21: Then those men were bound in their mantles, their tunics, their caps, and their garments, and were thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire.
verses.3:22: Because of this, since the king's command was urgent and the furnace was exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who carried up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
verses.3:23: And those three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell into the midst of the furnace of burning fire, bound.
verses.3:91: Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astounded and rose up in haste. He spoke up and said to his ministers, "Did we not throw three men into the midst of the fire, bound?" They answered and said to the king, "Certainly, King."
verses.3:92: He answered and said, "Look! I see four men unbound, walking about in the midst of the fire, and there is no harm on them; and the appearance of the fourth resembles a son of the gods."
verses.3:93: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the furnace of burning fire. He spoke up and said, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here!" Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the midst of the fire.
verses.3:94: And the satraps, the prefects, the governors, and the king's ministers gathered together and observed those men, that the fire had no power over their bodies: the hair of their heads was not singed, their mantles were not altered, and no smell of fire had come upon them.
verses.3:95: Nebuchadnezzar spoke up and said, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent His angel and rescued His servants who trusted in Him; they defied the king's command and surrendered their bodies so that they would not serve or worship any god except their own God.
verses.3:96: And by me a decree is issued that any people, nation, or language that speaks anything irreverent against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be cut limb from limb, and their house will be turned into a rubbish heap, because there is no other god who is able to deliver in this way."
verses.3:97: Then the king made Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego prosper in the province of Babylon.
verses.4:4: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was untroubled in my house and thriving in my palace.
verses.4:5: I saw a dream, and it terrified me, and the imaginings on my bed and the visions of my head alarmed me.
verses.4:10: And as for the visions of my head on my bed, I was watching, and look, a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was immense.
verses.4:11: The tree grew great and strong, and its height reached to the heavens, and the sight of it reached to the end of all the earth.
verses.4:12: Its foliage was lovely and its fruit was abundant, and in it was nourishment for all; beneath it the animals of the field found shade, and in its branches the birds of the heavens dwelt, and from it all flesh was nourished.
verses.4:13: I was watching in the visions of my head on my bed, and look, a watcher and holy one was descending from heaven.
verses.4:14: He called out loudly and spoke in this way: "Cut down the tree and sever its branches; strip off its foliage and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from beneath it and the birds from its branches.
verses.4:15: However, leave the stump of its roots in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, in the young grass of the field; and let him be soaked with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth.
verses.4:16: Let his heart be altered from that of a human, and let the heart of an animal be given to him, and let seven spans of time pass over him.
verses.4:17: The verdict is by the decree of the watchers, and the ruling is the word of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High is sovereign over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whomever He desires, and appoints the lowest of people over it."
verses.4:18: This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom are able to make the interpretation known to me, whereas you are capable, for a spirit of the holy gods is in you.
verses.4:19: Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stunned for a short while, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king responded and said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or the interpretation alarm you." Belteshazzar answered and said, "My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your foes.
verses.4:20: The tree that you saw, which grew great and strong, whose height reached to the heavens and the sight of it to all the earth,
verses.4:21: and whose foliage was lovely and its fruit was abundant, and in it was nourishment for all, beneath which the animals of the field dwelt and in whose branches the birds of the heavens settled,
verses.4:22: it is you, King, who have grown great and strong, and your greatness has grown and reached to the heavens, and your dominion to the end of the earth.
verses.4:23: And as for the king seeing a watcher and holy one descending from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it; however, leave the stump of its roots in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, in the young grass of the field, and let him be soaked with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the animals of the field until seven spans of time pass over him':
verses.4:24: this is the interpretation, King, and it is a decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:
verses.4:25: You will be driven away from mankind, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field, and you will be fed grass like oxen, and you will be soaked with the dew of heaven, and seven spans of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High is sovereign over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whomever He desires.
verses.4:26: And as for their saying to leave the stump of the roots of the tree, your kingdom will stand firm for you from the time you know that Heaven is sovereign.
verses.4:27: Therefore, King, may my counsel please you: break off your sins through righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor; perhaps there may be an extension of your tranquility."
verses.4:28: All of it came upon Nebuchadnezzar the king.
verses.4:29: At the end of twelve months, he was walking atop the royal palace of Babylon.
verses.4:30: The king answered and said, "Is this not great Babylon, which I myself built as a royal house by the strength of my power and for the honor of my majesty?"
verses.4:31: While the word was still in the king's mouth, a voice fell from heaven: "To you it is declared, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has passed from you,
verses.4:32: and you will be driven away from mankind, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field; you will be fed grass like oxen, and seven spans of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High is sovereign over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whomever He desires."
verses.4:33: At that very moment the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar, and he was driven away from mankind, and he ate grass like oxen, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like the feathers of eagles and his nails like the claws of birds.
verses.4:34: And at the close of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding came back to me; and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified the One who lives forever, because His dominion is an eternal dominion, and His kingdom lasts from generation to generation.
verses.4:36: At that very time my understanding came back to me, and for the honor of my kingdom, my majesty and my splendor came back to me; and my counselors and my nobles sought me out, and I was reinstated over my kingdom, and extraordinary greatness was added to me.
verses.4:37: King Nebuchadnezzar to all the peoples, nations, and languages who live in all the earth: May your peace multiply! It has pleased me to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed for me. His signs, how great they are, and His wonders, how powerful they are! His kingdom is an eternal kingdom, and His dominion lasts from generation to generation. Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, because all His deeds are truth and His ways are justice, and those who walk in pride He is able to bring low.
verses.5:1: Belshazzar the king made a great banquet for a thousand of his nobles, and in front of the thousand he was drinking wine.
verses.5:2: While tasting the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring the vessels of gold and silver that his father Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from the temple that was in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines, might drink out of them.
verses.5:3: Then they brought the vessels of gold that had been brought out from the temple of the house of God that was in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines, drank out of them.
verses.5:4: They drank the wine and gave praise to the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
verses.5:5: At that very moment fingers of a human hand came out and were writing opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace, and the king was watching the palm of the hand that was writing.
verses.5:6: Then the king's complexion changed, and his thoughts alarmed him; the joints of his hips were loosened, and his knees were knocking one against another.
verses.5:7: The king called out loudly to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the diviners. The king responded and said to the wise men of Babylon, "Anyone who reads this writing and declares its interpretation to me will wear purple and have a chain of gold around his neck, and will rule as third in the kingdom."
verses.5:8: Then all the wise men of the king came in, yet they were not able to read the writing or to make its interpretation known to the king.
verses.5:9: Then King Belshazzar became deeply alarmed, and his complexion was changing, and his nobles were bewildered.
verses.5:10: Because of the words of the king and his nobles, the queen entered the banquet hall. The queen responded and said, "King, live forever! Do not let your thoughts alarm you, and do not let your complexion change.
verses.5:11: There is a man in your kingdom in whom is a spirit of the holy gods, and in the days of your father illumination, discernment, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him; and King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners—your father the king.
verses.5:12: Because an extraordinary spirit, understanding, and discernment—interpreting dreams, explaining riddles, and untying knots—were found in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, now let Daniel be summoned, and he will declare the interpretation."
verses.5:13: Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king spoke up and said to Daniel, "Are you Daniel, one of the exiles of Judah whom the king my father brought from Judah?
verses.5:16: And I have heard about you that you are able to give interpretations and untie knots. Now if you are able to read the writing and make its interpretation known to me, you will wear purple and have a chain of gold around your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom."
verses.5:17: Then Daniel responded and said before the king, "May your gifts remain yours, and give your rewards to someone else; however, I will read the writing to the king and make the interpretation known to him.
verses.5:23: And you have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven, and they brought the vessels of His house before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines, were drinking wine out of them; and you gave praise to the gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which do not see, do not hear, and do not know, yet the God in whose hand is your breath, and to whom all your ways belong, you have not glorified.
verses.5:26: This is the interpretation of the word: 'Mene'—God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to a close.
verses.5:27: 'Tekel'—you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking.
verses.5:28: 'Peres'—your kingdom has been divided and given to Media and Persia."
verses.5:29: Then Belshazzar gave the order, and they clothed Daniel in purple, with a chain of gold around his neck, and proclaimed concerning him that he was to be the third ruler in the kingdom.
verses.5:30: On that same night Belshazzar, the Chaldean king, was killed.
verses.6:1: And Darius the Mede received the kingdom when he was about sixty-two years old.
verses.6:2: It pleased Darius to set one hundred twenty satraps over the kingdom, who were to be throughout the entire kingdom,
verses.6:3: and over them three chief officials, one of whom was Daniel, so that these satraps would give an account to them and the king would suffer no loss.
verses.6:4: Then this Daniel kept excelling above the chief officials and the satraps, because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king intended to set him over the whole kingdom.
verses.6:5: Then the chief officials and the satraps kept seeking to find a charge against Daniel regarding the kingdom, yet they could not find any charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found against him.
verses.6:6: Then those men said, "We will not find any charge against this Daniel unless we find it against him in the law of his God."
verses.6:7: Then these chief officials and satraps came thronging to the king and said to him, "King Darius, live forever!
verses.6:8: All the chief officials of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have taken counsel together to establish a royal statute and enforce an injunction that anyone who makes a petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you, King, shall be thrown into the den of lions.
verses.6:9: Now, King, establish the injunction and sign the document so that it may not be changed, according to the law of Media and Persia, which cannot be revoked."
verses.6:10: Because of this, King Darius signed the document and the injunction.
verses.6:11: Now when Daniel knew that the document had been signed, he entered his house, where he had open windows in his upper room facing Jerusalem, and three times a day he knelt on his knees, praying and giving thanks before his God, just as he had been doing before this.
verses.6:12: Then those men came thronging and found Daniel making petition and pleading for favor before his God.
verses.6:13: Then they came near and spoke before the king concerning the king's injunction, "Did you not sign an injunction that any man who petitions any god or man for thirty days, except to you, King, shall be thrown into the den of lions?" The king answered and said, "The matter stands firm, according to the law of Media and Persia, which cannot be revoked."
verses.6:14: Then they answered and said before the king, "Daniel, who is one of the exiles of Judah, pays no regard to you, King, or to the injunction that you signed, but three times a day he makes his petition."
verses.6:15: Then when the king heard this report, he was deeply distressed, and he set his mind on Daniel to rescue him; until sunset he kept exerting himself to deliver him.
verses.6:17: Then the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king spoke and said to Daniel, "Your God, whom you serve continually, may He rescue you!"
verses.6:18: And a stone was brought and laid over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing regarding Daniel could be changed.
verses.6:19: Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting; he had no entertainment brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.
verses.6:20: Then the king arose at daybreak, at the first light of dawn, and went in haste to the den of lions.
verses.6:21: When he came near the den, he cried out to Daniel with an anguished voice. The king spoke and said to Daniel, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?"
verses.6:22: Then Daniel spoke with the king, "King, live forever!
verses.6:23: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they have not harmed me, because innocence was found in me before Him; and before you as well, King, I have done no wrong."
verses.6:24: Then the king was overjoyed, and he ordered that Daniel be lifted up out of the den. So Daniel was lifted up out of the den, and no harm at all was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
verses.6:25: Then the king gave the order, and they brought those men who had maliciously accused Daniel and threw them, their children, and their wives into the den of lions; and they had not yet reached the bottom of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
verses.6:26: Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: "May your peace abound!
verses.6:27: A decree is issued by me that in every dominion of my kingdom people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; for He is the living God, enduring forever, His kingdom is one that will not be destroyed, and His dominion is to the end.
verses.6:28: He rescues and delivers, and He works signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, for He has rescued Daniel from the paw of the lions."
verses.6:29: So this Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
verses.7:1: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions in his head while on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream and told the summary of the matter.
verses.7:2: Daniel spoke up and said, "I was looking in my vision by night, and look, the four winds of heaven were churning up the great sea.
verses.7:3: And four great beasts were coming up out of the sea, different from one another.
verses.7:4: The first was like a lion and had wings of an eagle. I kept looking until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a man, and the heart of a man was given to it.
verses.7:5: And look, another beast, a second one, resembling a bear. It was raised up on one side, with three ribs in its mouth between its teeth, and they were saying to it, 'Rise up, devour much flesh!'
verses.7:6: After this I kept looking, and look, another one, like a leopard, and it had four wings of a bird on its back; the beast also had four heads, and dominion was given to it.
verses.7:7: After this I kept looking in the night visions, and look, a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and exceedingly strong, and it had great iron teeth; it was devouring and crushing, and trampling down the rest with its feet. It was different from all the beasts that were before it, and it had ten horns.
verses.7:8: While I was closely observing the horns, look, another horn, a small one, came up among them, and three of the first horns were uprooted before it; and look, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.
verses.7:9: I kept looking until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took His seat; His clothing was white like snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool; His throne was flames of fire, and its wheels were blazing fire.
verses.7:10: A river of fire was flowing and coming out from before Him; a thousand thousands were attending Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand were standing before Him. The court sat in session, and books were opened.
verses.7:11: Then I kept looking because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking; I kept looking until the beast was killed, and its body was destroyed and it was given over to the burning fire.
verses.7:12: As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, yet a prolongation of life was given to them for a time and a season.
verses.7:13: I kept looking in the night visions, and look, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming; he came up to the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before Him.
verses.7:14: And to him were given dominion, honor, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him; his dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will not be destroyed.
verses.7:15: As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed within its sheath, and the visions in my head kept alarming me.
verses.7:16: I approached one of those standing there and asked him the truth about all this. So he spoke to me and made known to me the interpretation of these matters:
verses.7:17: 'These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who will arise from the earth.
verses.7:18: But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.'
verses.7:19: Then I wanted to know the exact truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the rest, exceedingly terrifying, with its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze, devouring, crushing, and trampling down the remainder with its feet;
verses.7:20: and about the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn that came up, before which three fell, that horn which had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance was greater than its companions.
verses.7:21: I kept looking, and that horn was waging war with the holy ones and prevailing over them,
verses.7:22: until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given for the holy ones of the Most High, and the time arrived when the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
verses.7:23: This is what he said: 'As for the fourth beast, there will be a fourth kingdom on the earth that will be different from all the kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, tread it down, and crush it.
verses.7:24: As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings will arise; and another will arise after them, and he will be different from the former ones and will bring low three kings.
verses.7:25: He will speak words against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High, and he will intend to alter times and law; and they will be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time.
verses.7:26: But the court will sit in session, and his dominion will be taken away, to be annihilated and destroyed completely.
verses.7:27: Then the kingdom, the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High; His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey Him.'
verses.7:28: Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly alarmed me and my complexion changed, yet I kept the matter in my heart."
verses.8:1: In the third year of King Belshazzar's reign, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that appeared to me at the beginning.
verses.8:2: I looked in the vision, and it came about while I was looking that I was in Susa the citadel, which is in the province of Elam; and I looked in the vision, and I was by the Ulai canal.
verses.8:3: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was one ram standing in front of the canal, and it had two horns. The two horns were tall, yet one was taller than the other, and the taller one came up last.
verses.8:4: I saw the ram butting westward, northward, and southward, and no beasts could stand before it, nor was there anyone to rescue from its grasp; it acted according to its will and magnified itself.
verses.8:5: While I was pondering, look, a male goat was coming from the west across the face of the whole earth without touching the ground; and the goat had a prominent horn between its eyes.
verses.8:6: It came up to the ram with the two horns, which I had seen standing in front of the canal, and rushed at it in the fury of its strength.
verses.8:7: I saw it reach the side of the ram, and it raged furiously against it; it struck the ram and shattered its two horns, and the ram had no strength to stand before it. It hurled it down to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from its grasp.
verses.8:8: Then the male goat magnified itself exceedingly, yet when it became mighty, the great horn was broken; and in its place four prominent ones came up toward the four winds of heaven.
verses.8:9: From one of them came forth a single small horn, and it grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the Splendor.
verses.8:10: It grew up as far as the host of heaven, and it brought down to the earth some of the host and some of the stars and trampled them.
verses.8:11: It even magnified itself up to the Prince of the host; from Him the regular offering was removed, and the foundation of His sanctuary was thrown down.
verses.8:12: And a host was given over along with the regular offering through transgression; it threw truth down to the ground, and it acted and prospered.
verses.8:13: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to that certain one who was speaking, "How long is the vision of the regular offering and the transgression that brings desolation, giving over both the sanctuary and the host to trampling?"
verses.8:14: He said to me, "For two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be vindicated."
verses.8:15: Now when I, Daniel, had seen the vision and was seeking understanding, look, standing before me was one with the appearance of a man.
verses.8:16: And I heard a human voice from the midst of the Ulai, and it called out and said, "Gabriel, make this one understand the vision."
verses.8:17: So he came near to where I was standing, and as he approached, I was terrified and fell upon my face. Then he said to me, "Understand, son of man, for the vision is for the time of the end."
verses.8:18: Now while he was speaking with me, I sank into a deep sleep with my face to the ground; yet he touched me and set me upright where I had been standing.
verses.8:19: He said, "Look, I am about to make known to you what will happen in the latter period of the indignation, for it is for the appointed time of the end.
verses.8:20: The ram that you saw with the two horns—they are the kings of Media and Persia.
verses.8:21: And the shaggy male goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn that is between its eyes is the first king.
verses.8:22: As for the one that was broken, with four arising in its place, four kingdoms will arise from the nation, yet not with his strength.
verses.8:23: In the latter period of their kingdom, when the transgressors have reached their fullness, a fierce-faced king who understands riddles will arise.
verses.8:24: His strength will become mighty, yet not by his own strength; he will destroy to an astonishing degree, and he will prosper and take action, destroying mighty ones and the people of the holy ones.
verses.8:25: Through his shrewdness he will cause deceit to prosper by his hand; in his heart he will magnify himself, and amid security he will destroy many. He will even stand against the Prince of princes, yet without a hand he will be broken.
verses.8:26: And the vision of the evening and the morning that was spoken is true; but as for you, seal up the vision, for it concerns many days."
verses.8:27: Then I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay sick for days. Afterward I got up and performed the king's work, yet I was appalled at the vision, and there was no one who understood.
verses.9:1: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, from the lineage of Media, who was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
verses.9:2: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, perceived in the books the number of the years concerning which the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah the prophet, that seventy years must be fulfilled for the ruins of Jerusalem.
verses.9:3: So I set my face toward the Lord God to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
verses.9:4: I prayed to the LORD my God and made confession, saying, "Please, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and loyal love for those who love Him and keep His commandments,
verses.9:5: we have sinned and committed iniquity, acted wickedly and rebelled, and turned aside from Your commandments and from Your ordinances.
verses.9:6: We have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.
verses.9:7: To You, Lord, belongs righteousness, yet to us belongs shame of face, as on this day—to the men of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, those who are near and those who are far off in all the lands where You have driven them, because of their unfaithfulness with which they acted unfaithfully against You.
verses.9:8: LORD, to us belongs shame of face, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against You.
verses.9:9: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against Him
verses.9:10: and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God, to walk in His laws which He set before us by the hand of His servants the prophets.
verses.9:11: All Israel has transgressed Your law and turned aside so as not to obey Your voice; therefore the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out upon us, because we have sinned against Him.
verses.9:12: He has confirmed His word that He spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing upon us a great calamity; for under all heaven nothing has been done like what has been done in Jerusalem.
verses.9:13: Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all this calamity has come upon us; yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquity and gaining insight into Your truth.
verses.9:14: Therefore the LORD kept watch over the calamity and brought it upon us; for the LORD our God is righteous in all His works that He has done, yet we have not obeyed His voice.
verses.9:15: And now, Lord our God, who brought Your people out from the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made a name for Yourself, as on this day—we have sinned, we have done wickedly.
verses.9:16: Lord, in accordance with all Your righteous acts, please let Your anger and Your wrath turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a reproach to all who surround us.
verses.9:17: And now, our God, listen to the prayer of Your servant and to his supplications, and cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary, for the Lord's sake.
verses.9:18: Incline Your ear, my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see our desolations and the city over which Your name is called. For we are not laying our supplications before You on the basis of our righteous acts, but on the basis of Your abundant mercies.
verses.9:19: Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, pay heed and act! Do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, because Your name is called over Your city and over Your people."
verses.9:20: Now while I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and laying my supplication before the LORD my God on behalf of the holy mountain of my God—
verses.9:21: while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, reached me in swift flight about the time of the evening offering.
verses.9:22: He gave instruction and spoke with me, saying, "Daniel, now I have come forth to instruct you in understanding.
verses.9:23: At the beginning of your supplications a word went forth, and I have come to declare it, for you are greatly treasured. So ponder the word and discern the vision.
verses.9:24: Seventy weeks have been decreed upon your people and upon your holy city, to restrain the transgression, to bring sin to an end, to atone for iniquity, to bring in eternal righteousness, to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a holy of holies.
verses.9:25: So know and gain insight: from the going forth of a word to restore and to build Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, there will be seven weeks; and for sixty-two weeks it will be built again, with plaza and moat, though in distress of the times.
verses.9:26: After the sixty-two weeks, an anointed one will be cut off, and there will be nothing for him; and the people of the coming prince will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will be with a flood, and until the end of the war desolations are decreed.
verses.9:27: And he will make a covenant strong with the many for one week, and for half of the week he will cause sacrifice and grain offering to cease; and upon the wing of abominations will be a desolator, until the decreed complete destruction is poured out upon the desolator."
verses.10:1: In the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. The message was true and involved a great conflict; he understood the message, and understanding came to him in the vision.
verses.10:2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks.
verses.10:3: I ate no choice food, neither meat nor wine came into my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all until three full weeks were fulfilled.
verses.10:4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was along the bank of the great river, which is the Tigris.
verses.10:5: I raised my eyes and looked, and look, there was a certain man dressed in linen, whose waist was belted with fine gold of Uphaz.
verses.10:6: His body resembled beryl, his face had the look of lightning, his eyes were like torches of fire, his arms and legs had the luster of polished bronze, and the sound of his words resembled the sound of a multitude.
verses.10:7: I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision; yet a great trembling fell over them, so they fled to hide themselves.
verses.10:8: So I was left by myself and looked at this great vision. No strength was left in me; my vigor turned to ruin within me, and I retained no strength.
verses.10:9: Then I heard the sound of his words, and as I heard the sound of his words, I sank into a deep sleep on my face, with my face toward the ground.
verses.10:10: Then look, a hand touched me and set me trembling onto my knees and the palms of my hands.
verses.10:11: He said to me, "Daniel, greatly treasured man, understand the words that I am speaking to you and stand upright in your place, for I have now been sent to you." As he spoke this word with me, I stood up trembling.
verses.10:12: Then he said to me, "Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come on account of your words.
verses.10:13: Yet the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood opposing me for twenty-one days; then look, Michael, one of the foremost princes, came to help me, and I was left there beside the kings of Persia.
verses.10:14: Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision still pertains to days to come."
verses.10:15: When he spoke with me according to these words, I set my face toward the ground and became speechless.
verses.10:16: Then look, one in the likeness of the sons of man touched my lips. I opened my mouth and spoke, saying to the one standing before me, "My lord, because of the vision, pangs of anguish have come upon me, and I have retained no strength.
verses.10:17: How can this servant of my lord speak with my lord here? As for me, right now no strength remains in me, and no breath is left in me."
verses.10:18: Then one who had the appearance of a man touched me again and strengthened me.
verses.10:19: He said, "Do not be afraid, greatly treasured man. Peace be to you; be strong, yes, be strong." As he spoke with me, I gained strength and said, "Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me."
verses.10:20: Then he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I go out, look, the prince of Greece is coming.
verses.10:21: Nevertheless, I will tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth. Yet there is no one who stands firmly with me against these except Michael, your prince."
verses.11:1: "And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to strengthen him and be a stronghold for him.
verses.11:2: Now I will tell you the truth. Look, three more kings will arise for Persia, and the fourth will acquire greater wealth than all of them; and when he grows strong through his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
verses.11:3: Then a mighty king will arise; he will rule with a vast dominion and do according to his will.
verses.11:4: Yet as soon as he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not to his descendants, nor with the dominion by which he ruled, for his kingdom will be uprooted and pass to others besides these.
verses.11:5: Then the king of the south will grow strong, yet one of his princes will grow stronger than he and will rule; his dominion will be a vast dominion.
verses.11:6: At the end of some years they will form an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an equitable agreement. Yet she will not retain the strength of her arm, nor will he stand, nor his arm; she will be given over, along with those who brought her, the one who fathered her, and the one who supported her in those times.
verses.11:7: Then a shoot from her roots will arise in his place; he will advance against the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north, and he will deal with them and prevail.
verses.11:8: He will also carry off their gods into captivity to Egypt, together with their cast images and their precious vessels of silver and gold; and for some years he will hold back from the king of the north.
verses.11:9: Then he will come into the kingdom of the king of the south, yet he will return to his own land.
verses.11:10: His sons will mobilize for war and gather a multitude of great forces; and he will surely come, overflow, and pass through, and he will return and press the war all the way to his fortress.
verses.11:11: Then the king of the south will be enraged and will march out and fight with him, with the king of the north; he will marshal a vast multitude, yet the multitude will be given into his hand.
verses.11:12: When the multitude is carried off, his heart will be lifted up; he will bring down tens of thousands, yet he will not prevail.
verses.11:13: Then the king of the north will again marshal a multitude greater than the first; and at the end of the times, some years later, he will surely come with a great army and abundant supplies.
verses.11:14: In those times many will rise up against the king of the south, and violent men among your people will lift themselves up to establish a vision, but they will stumble.
verses.11:15: Then the king of the north will come, heap up a siege ramp, and capture a city of fortifications. The forces of the south will not stand, nor even his choicest troops, for there will be no strength to stand.
verses.11:16: The one who comes against him will do according to his will, and no one will stand before him; he will take his stand in the land of splendor, with destruction in his hand.
verses.11:17: He will set his face to come with the might of his whole kingdom, and he will make equitable terms with him; he will also give him the daughter of women to ruin it, yet it will not stand, nor will it be for him.
verses.11:18: Then he will set his face toward the coastlands and capture many of them. Yet a commander will put an end to his reproach against him; moreover, he will turn his reproach back upon him.
verses.11:19: Then he will turn his face back toward the fortresses of his own land, yet he will stumble and fall and will not be found.
verses.11:20: Then in his place one will arise who sends an exactor through the splendor of the kingdom; yet within a few days he will be broken, neither in anger nor in battle.
verses.11:21: In his place a despised person will arise, upon whom royal majesty has not been bestowed; he will come in a time of tranquility and seize the kingdom through flatteries.
verses.11:22: The sweeping forces will be swept away from before him and broken, as well as the prince of the covenant.
verses.11:23: From the time an alliance is made with him, he will practice deceit; he will rise up and become mighty with a small nation.
verses.11:24: In a time of tranquility he will enter the richest parts of the province, and he will do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers did: he will scatter plunder, spoil, and goods among them. He will also devise his schemes against fortified places, yet for a time.
verses.11:25: He will stir up his strength and his heart against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south will mobilize for battle with an exceedingly great and mighty army; yet he will not stand, for they will devise schemes against him.
verses.11:26: Those who eat his royal food will break him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall mortally wounded.
verses.11:27: As for both kings, their hearts will be bent on doing harm, and at one table they will speak falsehood; yet it will not succeed, for the end is still for the appointed time.
verses.11:28: Then he will return to his land with great wealth, with his heart set against the holy covenant; he will take action and return to his own land.
verses.11:29: At the appointed time he will return and come into the south, yet this latter time will not turn out like the former.
verses.11:30: For ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will be disheartened; he will turn back and rage against the holy covenant and take action. He will turn back and pay regard to those who forsake the holy covenant.
verses.11:31: Forces from him will arise and profane the sanctuary, the fortress; they will remove the regular offering and set up the desolating abomination.
verses.11:32: He will corrupt through flattery those who act wickedly against the covenant, yet the people who know their God will prove strong and act.
verses.11:33: Those with insight among the people will bring understanding to the many; yet they will stumble by sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, for days.
verses.11:34: When they stumble, they will be helped with a little help, and many will join themselves to them with flatteries.
verses.11:35: Some of those with insight will stumble, in order to refine them, purify them, and make them white until the time of the end, for it is still for the appointed time.
verses.11:36: Then the king will do according to his will; he will lift himself up and magnify himself above every god, and against the God of gods he will speak astounding things. He will succeed until the indignation comes to an end, for what is determined will be carried out.
verses.11:37: He will pay no regard to the gods of his fathers; neither to the desire of women nor to any god will he pay regard, for he will magnify himself above all.
verses.11:38: Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses; a god whom his fathers did not know he will honor with gold and silver, with costly stones and precious things.
verses.11:39: He will take action against the strongest fortresses with a foreign god; for those whom he acknowledges he will increase honor, he will make them rule over the many, and he will apportion land for a price.
verses.11:40: At the time of the end, the king of the south will clash with him, and the king of the north will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships; he will enter countries, overflow, and pass through.
verses.11:41: He will also enter the land of splendor, and many will stumble; yet these will escape from his hand: Edom, Moab, and the foremost of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:42: He will stretch out his hand against the countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
verses.11:43: He will rule over the hidden treasures of gold and silver and over all the precious things of Egypt, and Libyans and Cushites will be at his steps.
verses.11:44: Yet reports from the east and from the north will alarm him, and he will march out in great fury to exterminate and utterly destroy many.
verses.11:45: He will pitch the tents of his royal pavilion between the seas and the holy mountain of splendor; yet he will come to his end, and there will be no one to help him."
verses.12:1: "And at that time Michael will stand up, the great prince who stands watch over the sons of your people. And there will be a time of distress such as has not happened since a nation came to be until that time; yet at that time your people will be delivered, each one found written in the book.
verses.12:2: And many of those who sleep in the ground of dust will awaken, these to eternal life, and those to disgrace, to eternal abhorrence.
verses.12:3: And those with insight will shine like the radiance of the expanse, and those who bring the many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.
verses.12:4: And as for you, Daniel, shut away the words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will roam back and forth, and knowledge will multiply."
verses.12:5: Then I, Daniel, looked, and here were two others standing, one on this side at the bank of the river, and one on that side at the bank of the river.
verses.12:6: And one said to the man wearing linen, who was above the waters of the river, "How long until the end of the wonders?"
verses.12:7: And I heard the man wearing linen, who was above the waters of the river, as he lifted his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by the One who lives forever, "It will be for an appointed time, appointed times, and a half; and as soon as the shattering of the power of the holy people is finished, all these things will be finished."
verses.12:8: And I heard, yet I did not understand, so I said, "My lord, what is the outcome of these things?"
verses.12:9: And he said, "Go, Daniel, for the words are shut away and sealed until the time of the end.
verses.12:10: Many will be purified, whitened, and refined, while the wicked will behave wickedly; and not one of the wicked will understand, but those with insight will understand.
verses.12:11: And from the time the regular offering is removed and the desolating abomination is set in place, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
verses.12:12: Blessed is the one who keeps waiting and reaches one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
verses.12:13: But as for you, go to the end; and you will rest, and you will rise to your allotted share at the end of the days."

notes.1:3: Hebrew sarisim can denote either literal eunuchs or high royal court officials (cf. Gen 39:1).
notes.1:10: The Piel verb rendered 'make ... forfeit' occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible, reflecting an Aramaic legal term meaning 'render guilty or liable.'
notes.1:11: Hebrew hammeltsar carries the definite article and is an official title (from Akkadian massaru, 'guardian' or 'attendant'), not a personal name.
notes.1:20: Literally 'ten hands,' a Hebrew idiom expressing a tenfold measure or degree (cf. Gen 43:34).
notes.2:1: Shenatho nihyethah alaw is literally "his sleep was upon him" or "came to an end on him"; the sense is that he could not sleep.
notes.2:2: The four classes are chartummim (magicians), ashshafim (enchanters or conjurers), mekhashshefim (sorcerers) and kasdim (Chaldeans, here a class of learned diviners).
notes.2:4: The Hebrew narrative switches to Aramaic after "in Aramaic"; the Aramaic continues through 7:28. Ketiv l'bdyk / qere le'avdakh both mean "to your servants"; the qere is translated.
notes.2:5: Ketiv/qere differ only in the spelling of "to the Chaldeans." Azda is a Persian loanword probably meaning "certain, publicly announced" (older translations took it as "gone"). Haddamin tit'avdun is literally "you will be made into pieces." Newali means "refuse heap."
notes.2:8: Idanna antun zavnin is literally "you are buying the time," that is, stalling.
notes.2:9: Chadah-hi dathkhon is literally "one is your law," meaning there is only one verdict for you. The Hithpael qere hizdemintun ("you have conspired / agreed together") is translated in place of the Haphel ketiv hizmantun ("you have prepared/planned").
notes.2:10: The ketiv/qere difference is only in the spelling of "Chaldeans." Kol-qovel di is a recurring Aramaic connective meaning "because, since, just as."
notes.2:14: Rav-tabbachayya is literally "chief of the slaughterers"; the title came to mean the commander of the royal bodyguard.
notes.2:18: Elah shemayya, rendered "the God of heaven," is a regular title in Persian-period Aramaic; shemayya has the same plural form as Hebrew shamayim.
notes.2:22: The qere nehora ("light") is translated; the ketiv differs only in spelling.
notes.2:25: Bene galutha di Yehud is literally "the sons of the exile of Judah."
notes.2:26: The ketiv/qere difference (ha'ithakh, "are you") is one of spelling only.
notes.2:27: Gazrin, literally "cutters/deciders," are probably astrologers or diviners who determine fates.
notes.2:28: Be'acharith yomayya is literally "in the end of the days." The "visions of your head" are what passed through his mind.
notes.2:29: The qere ant ("you") is translated, and likewise in 2:31, 2:37 and 2:38. "He who uncovers mysteries" (gale razayya) refers to God, so the pronoun is capitalized.
notes.2:31: Wa'alu is an Aramaic interjection like "look!" (equivalent to Hebrew hinneh); it is rendered "and look."
notes.2:33: Chasaf is clay or earthenware; the qere forms minnehen (feminine "some of them") are translated as "part ... part" (and likewise in 2:41 and 2:42).
notes.2:38: Bene anasha is literally "sons of men" (human beings), here paired with wild animals and birds as what God places in the king's hand. The qere dayerin ("dwell") is translated.
notes.2:39: The qere ara' ("lower, inferior") replaces ketiv ar'a (which resembles the emphatic noun "earth"), while qere telitha'ah ("third") differs from the ketiv only in spelling.
notes.2:41: Nitsbetha means firmness or hardness. Chasaf di-fechar is "potter's clay," and chasaf tina is "clay of mud."
notes.2:43: The qere wedi ("and as") is translated. "Mix themselves with the seed of men" probably refers to intermarriage between royal houses, but the Aramaic is kept literal.
notes.2:46: Segid means to bow down or pay homage; "bowed down" keeps the act without deciding on its theology. Nichochin are pleasing or soothing aromas (incense).
notes.2:47: Mare malkhin is rendered "Lord of kings" because it refers to God.
notes.2:48: Rabbi is "made great," that is, promoted. Rav-signin is "chief of the prefects."
notes.2:49: Bithra malka is literally "in the gate of the king," meaning the royal court where officials served.
notes.3:8: Literally 'ate the pieces of the Jews,' an Aramaic and Akkadian idiom meaning to slander or bring malicious accusations.
notes.3:12: The translation follows the Qere singular 'your god' (as also in 3:18); the Ketiv reads plural 'your gods' (contrast the unambiguous plural 'my gods' in 3:14).
notes.3:15: The Aramaic conditional sentence leaves its positive outcome unstated (aposiopesis), breaking directly into the warning 'but if you do not worship.'
notes.3:17: Following the Masoretic accentuation, Aramaic hen itay is rendered 'if it is so,' with both prepositional phrases governed by the second verb 'rescue'; alternatively, the clause may be construed as 'if our God whom we serve is able to rescue us, He will rescue us.'
notes.3:92: Literally 'a son of gods,' a Semitic idiom used by the pagan king for a divine or angelic being (cf. 'His angel' in 3:95). Verses 3:91-97 correspond to MT 3:24-30.
notes.4:13: "watcher and holy one": Aramaic ir weqaddish uses an epexegetical conjunction (confirmed by the singular participle nachit, "descending") to designate a single vigilant heavenly messenger.
notes.4:19: "those who hate you ... your foes": The Ketiv writes the plural 2ms suffix -ayk (lsn'yk, l'ryk), while the Qere reads -ak (lesane'ak, le'arak), a Tiberian Aramaic suffix variant that coincides with the singular form (similarly on plural nouns in 4:27 and 5:23). "a short while": Aramaic sha'ah denotes a brief moment or interval rather than a sixty-minute hour (cf. 4:33; 5:5).
notes.4:26: "Heaven is sovereign": Aramaic shemayya ("the heavens," grammatically plural with the plural adjective shallitin) serves here as a reverent metonymy for God.
notes.4:27: "my counsel ... break off": Aramaic milki ("my counsel") plays on malka ("King"), and the Peal imperative peruq ("break off" or "redeem") conveys either casting away sins or redeeming them through righteous conduct.
notes.4:37: Following the Saints verse arrangement, this verse carries Nebuchadnezzar's greeting and opening doxology (Masoretic 3:31-33; traditional English 4:1-3) before his closing praise (Masoretic 4:34; traditional English 4:37).
notes.5:5: "fingers ... came out": Following the Qere nepaqah (Peal perfect 3fp), which agrees with the feminine plural subject "fingers," whereas the Ketiv reads masculine plural npqw. "palm of the hand": Aramaic pas yeda refers to the flat portion of the hand from wrist to fingers.
notes.5:6: "the joints of his hips were loosened": Aramaic qitrei chartseh mishtarayin (literally "the knots of his loins were untied," Hithpeel participle of shera) sets up an ironic wordplay with Daniel's reputation for "untying knots" (qitrin, shera) in 5:12 and 5:16.
notes.5:7: "third in the kingdom": Aramaic talti (and talta in 5:16, 29) means "third" or "third ruler."
notes.5:8: "its interpretation": Following the Qere ufishreh ("and its interpretation") rather than the Ketiv wpsr' ("and the interpretation").
notes.6:7: Aramaic hargishu (Haphel of rgsh, also in 6:12) literally means "came thronging" or "crowded in noisily"; some take it as "acted in concert."
notes.6:17: The Aramaic imperfect yeshezivinnakh (Shaphel of shyzb) can express either a wish ("may He rescue you") or a confident statement ("He will rescue you").
notes.6:19: The meaning of the rare Aramaic noun dachawan is uncertain; proposals include "entertainment," "diversions," "musical instruments," "concubines," or "food."
notes.6:25: Literally "who had eaten the pieces of Daniel," a standard Aramaic and Akkadian legal idiom meaning "maliciously accused" or "slandered."
notes.7:4: Here and in 7:5-8, 19-20, the Qere regularly uses the assimilated third-feminine-singular suffix -ah on plural nouns and prepositions where the Ketiv preserves the consonantal yod (-yh); in 7:6, the Qere reads singular "its back" (gabbah) against Ketiv "its backs/sides."
notes.7:9: Aramaic remiw (Peil passive of rmh, "throw, cast") here carries the idiomatic sense "were set in place," referring to the placing of thrones for judgment.
notes.7:13: Aramaic kevar enash literally means "like a son of man," an idiom for a human figure in contrast to the preceding beasts.
notes.7:15: Aramaic nidneh is a Persian loanword meaning "sheath," used metaphorically here for the human body containing the spirit.
notes.7:27: Aramaic elyonin ("the Most High," also in 7:18, 22, 25) is a plural of majesty; the singular suffix on "His kingdom" and "Him" refers either to the Most High or to the collective singular noun "people."
notes.8:9: Hebrew "mitztze'irah" literally means "from smallness" or "rather small." "The Splendor" translates Hebrew "hatztzevi," an epithet for the land of Israel (cf. Dan 11:16, 41).
notes.8:11: Ketiv reads Hiphil active "herim" ("it removed"), while Qere (translated here) reads Hophal passive "huram" ("was removed"). Hebrew "hattamid" ("the continual") refers to the regular daily burnt offering.
notes.8:12: The compressed Hebrew clause "vetzava tinnaten al-hattamid befasha" treats "tzava" ("host") as feminine and can be construed either as the host being handed over along with the regular offering because of transgression, or as a hostile force being set over the regular offering in rebellion.
notes.8:14: Hebrew "venitzdaq" is the sole Niphal occurrence of the root "tzadaq" in the Hebrew Bible, denoting being set right, vindicated, or restored to its rightful state. The Masoretic text reads "to me" ("elay") rather than "to him."
notes.9:12: Ketiv reads plural "devarav" ("His words"), while Qere (translated here) reads singular "devaro" ("His word").
notes.9:21: Hebrew "mu'af bi'af" is lexically uncertain; deriving it from "uf" (Hophal participle) with "ye'af" yields "in swift flight," whereas connecting it to "ya'ef" yields "in utter weariness."
notes.9:24: Two Ketiv/Qere variants appear in the second infinitive clause: Ketiv reads "velachtom chatta'ot" ("and to seal up sins"), while Qere (translated here) reads Hiphil "ulehatem chatta't" ("and to bring sin to an end"). Hebrew "shavu'im" ("weeks") denotes periods of seven, and "nechtakh" ("have been decreed") is a Niphal hapax legomenon.
notes.9:25: The Masoretic disjunctive accent (athnach) separates "seven weeks" from "sixty-two weeks," linking the sixty-two weeks to the rebuilding; without that pause, "seven weeks and sixty-two weeks" together measure the span until an anointed prince. Hebrew "mashiach" literally means "anointed one" (echoing "anoint" in v. 24).
notes.9:27: The phrase "al kenaf shiqqutzim meshomem" ("upon the wing of abominations [will be] a desolator") is syntactically compressed and may refer to a pinnacle or extremity of the temple defiled by appalling abominations. At the end of the verse, Qal participle "shomem" can be read actively ("the desolator") or passively ("the desolate one").
notes.10:1: Hebrew tsava gadol literally means "great warfare" or "great hardship," pointing to the severity of the conflict revealed in the message.
notes.10:2: Hebrew literally reads "three weeks, days," adding "days" in apposition to specify three full weeks of days rather than weeks of years.
notes.10:4: Hebrew Hiddekel, the ancient name of the Tigris River.
notes.10:16: Literally "my pangs have turned upon me," an idiom using the noun for labor pains to express sudden, overwhelming anguish (cf. 1 Sam 4:19).
notes.11:6: Masoretic vocalization reads ha-yoldah (Qal active participle with 3fs suffix), "the one who fathered her," rather than "her child"; likewise "his arm" translates the MT text (uzero'o) rather than an emendation to "his offspring."
notes.11:8: Hebrew ya'amod min literally means "stand away from" (hold back from); alternatively, the preposition may be taken comparatively as "outlast the king of the north."
notes.11:10: Following the Qere (veyitgareh, 3ms Hithpael imperfect, "he will press the war"); the Ketiv (vyitgaru) reads a 3mp plural ("they will wage war").
notes.11:12: Following the Qere (veram, waw + Qal perfect); the Ketiv (yarum) reads a Qal imperfect with essentially the same meaning ("his heart will be lifted up").
notes.11:17: The feminine singular suffixes in "to ruin it" and "it will not stand, nor will it be for him" may refer either to the southern kingdom/scheme or to the daughter herself ("she will not stand, nor will she be for him").
notes.11:18: Following the Qere (veyasem, "he will set [his face]"); the Ketiv (vyashev) reads "he will turn [his face]" (as in v. 19). Hebrew bilti here carries an emphatic adversative sense ("moreover, indeed").
notes.11:39: Following the Qere (yakkir, Hiphil imperfect, "whom he acknowledges"); the Ketiv (hikkir) reads a Hiphil perfect ("whom he acknowledged"). The clause may also be understood as "those who acknowledge him."
notes.12:2: Hebrew admat-afar is a construct phrase meaning literally "ground of dust" (an image for the grave). The rare noun diraon ("abhorrence") occurs elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible only in Isaiah 66:24.
notes.12:7: The Masoretic Text vocalizes moadim as plural ("appointed times"), often understood as two times (parallel to Aramaic Dan 7:25). Hebrew pairs the Piel infinitive construct of kalah ("finishing" the shattering of the "hand," i.e., power) with its Qal imperfect ("will be finished").
notes.12:10: The first two verbs (from barar and laban) are Hithpael forms paired with a Niphal passive (from tsaraph); in Late Biblical Hebrew the Hithpael frequently carries a passive sense ("be purified, whitened"), though a reflexive nuance ("purify themselves") is also possible.
notes.12:11: Hebrew hatamid ("the continual") is used substantively in Daniel for the daily temple offering. The phrase shiquts shomem combines "abomination/detestable thing" with the Qal participle of shamem ("desolating" or "appalling").
notes.12:13: Hebrew hayamin ("the days") uses the Aramaic masculine plural ending -in rather than the standard Hebrew -im, a notable Aramaism in the final word of the book. The noun goral ("lot") denotes an allotted share or inheritance.

unplaced.text: So a decree was issued by me to bring before me all the wise men of Babylon, so that they would make the interpretation of the dream known to me.
Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the diviners came in, and I told the dream before them, yet they did not make its interpretation known to me.
And at last Daniel came in before me—whose name is Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and in whom is a spirit of the holy gods—and I told the dream before him:
"Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, since I know that a spirit of the holy gods is in you and no mystery perplexes you, tell me the visions of my dream that I saw and its interpretation."
unplaced.note: Alternatively, "as for the visions of my dream that I saw, tell me its interpretation."

unplaced.text: And all the inhabitants of the earth are regarded as nothing, and He acts according to His will among the host of heaven and the inhabitants of the earth; and there is no one who can restrain His hand or say to Him, "What have You done?"
unplaced.note: Literally "strike against His hand," an Aramaic idiom for restraining or halting someone's action.

unplaced.text: And I have heard about you that a spirit of the gods is in you, and that enlightenment, discernment, and surpassing wisdom have been found in you.

And now the wise men, the enchanters, were brought in before me so that they would read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, yet they were not able to declare the interpretation of the matter.
As for you, King, the Most High God gave kingship, greatness, glory, and splendor to Nebuchadnezzar your father.

And because of the greatness that He gave him, all the peoples, nations, and languages were trembling and afraid before him. Whomever he wished, he put to death; and whomever he wished, he kept alive; and whomever he wished, he lifted up; and whomever he wished, he brought low.
But when his heart grew proud and his spirit became hardened to act arrogantly, he was brought down from the throne of his kingdom, and his glory was removed from him.

And he was driven away from human beings, and his heart was made like that of the wild animals, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys; he was fed grass like oxen, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until he came to know that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humanity and appoints whomever He wishes over it.
But you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, although you knew all of this.
Then the hand was sent from before Him, and this writing was inscribed.
And this is the writing that was inscribed: 'Mene, Mene, Tekel, and Parsin.'
unplaced.note: The Aramaic words name weights—mina, shekel, and half-minas (plural parsin, preceded by u-, "and")—which Daniel explains in 5:26-28 by wordplay on cognate verbs ("numbered," "weighed," "divided," using singular Peres) and the name Paras ("Persia").

unplaced.text: Then those men came thronging to the king and said to the king, "Know, King, that it is a law of Media and Persia that no ban or statute the king establishes can be changed."
